uncited: *   **Time Complexity:** Quantization is $O(N)$ where $N=240$ is the number of normals, or $O(1)$ if a spatial hash or lookup table is used to map vectors to indices.
*   **Memory Complexity:** The quantization table requires storage for 240 vectors.
If stored as 3 floats per vector, this is $240 \times 12 = 2880$ bytes.
If stored as indices into a 256-entry color map, it is negligible.
*   **When to use:** When a static, uniform normal quantization is sufficient and hardware supports 256-entry color maps.
*   **When not to use:** When data-dependent optimization is required for better visual quality (use Simulated Annealing variant) or when higher precision is needed.
